text:
jordan: Heads up — ACME Engineering opened a high-severity ticket: they started seeing a 15-25% spike in 429s right after the rate policy push at 09:00 UTC. Says errors cluster on short 10-30s bursts. Attaching customer logs they pasted.

maya: Ack, can you drop the snippet here? Do we know if they were on the canary percent or prod? :eyes:

jordan: They were routed to the new limit set (canary 25%) per our rollout. Log line from their app: {"status":429,"msg":"rate_limit_exceeded","retry_after":2} — pattern is abrupt rejects during short concurrent bursts, then recovers. Customer also says billing shows spikes in "requests" but token usage steady.

eva: @maya @sam thanks for tagging. Two quick hypotheses: 1) burst grace window got tightened in the new policy (prefill/k-values), 2) our burst accounting mapping (client->bucket) changed for their client_id. I just checked rollout: canary was at 25% at 09:00, and we pushed another 25% at 09:20 (deploy-bot logs).

sre-bot: policy-rollout-bot: rate_policy_v3 deployed to canary=25% at 2026-03-15T09:00:12Z; canary increased to 50% at 2026-03-15T09:20:04Z.

sam: I can reproduce locally with a short script that opens 40 concurrent connections for 20s against a canary endpoint. Repro commands: 
for i in {1..40}; do curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"x","max_tokens":16}' &
done
wait
I see a flurry of 429s at ~5-7s and then a carryover of quick retries hitting quota counters.

maya: Good repro. Customer timeline matches: spike -> retries -> more 429s. Billing spike could be retries being counted as requests. We should confirm retry deduping behavior for 429s.

lee: From CS perspective, customer is asking for either an immediate rollback of the canary or a temporary exception for their org_id. They are worried about user-facing errors in their app. Suggested interim: enable a soft fallback (higher burst cap) for their org_id until fix.

eva: Two parallel actions I propose: (A) rollback canary from 50% -> 25% immediately (manual) and (B) create a temporary org-level override for ACME with increased burst_grace window. Sam, can you prepare the patch/flag for override? Maya, can you coordinate the rollback if eng-platform approves?

sam: I can add an override flag keyed to org_id in the routing layer within 15 min. Will push a knob behind feature-flag. Patch will include: override{org_id: 'acme-corp', burst_grace_ms: 5000}. I'll post PR link.

maya: I'll hold on rollback until we confirm override is ready. If PR blocks, we'll roll back canary to 0% and pin to previous policy. @eva do you have the rollback runbook handy?

eva: Rollback runbook (short): 
1) Pause rollout in console -> set canary to previous version (rate_policy_v2).
2) Verify latency/429 metrics for 5 minutes in /metrics/rl/429_rate by canary-tag. 
3) Notify support+cs and mark incident. 
I can initiate step 1 in 5 mins if needed.

sre-bot: metrics-alert: rl.429_rate increased by 18% across canary hosts starting 2026-03-15T09:05Z.

jordan: Customer requested a tight SLA: roll back if errors don't drop within 10 mins of override. They also want us to investigate billing counts (retries counting). Can we confirm whether retries triggered by 429s are billed as separate requests or deduped within 30s?

sam: Quick answer: requests are metered per HTTP request; retries are counted. There's a throttling middleware that can mark retry headers, but billing currently counts each successful token generation call. For 429s that never succeed, they still count as requests in the request-metering. We'll add a doc note but for now they explain billing spike.

eva: OK plan: Sam will push org override; Maya will hold rollback and monitor; I will throttle the canary growth to stop further expansion; Jordan/Lee to keep ACME informed and offer temporary override as option.

maya: Noted. I'll post status back in 10 min with metrics snapshot.

jordan: ACME replied — they accepted temporary override and asked for ETA. I'll tell them ~20-30 min until override flag is live, or immediate rollback if it's not fast enough.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: override flag PR opened by sam - https://git.internal/pr/4521 ; CI started.

sam: CI passed. Merging now, will enable flag for org_id=acme-corp in config service.

sre-bot: config-service: override enabled for org_id=acme-corp (burst_grace_ms=5000).

maya: Override applied. Early signal: 429 rate for acme org dropped ~70% within 2 mins. :thumbsup:

lee: Customer on call confirmed errors mostly cleared. They're asking for root cause postmortem and whether the rollout had different burst mapping rules.

eva: We'll schedule a short follow-up postmortem. Initial root cause hypothesis: new policy reduced tolerated per-client burst tokens due to a change in bucket attribution logic; combined with client retry patterns caused amplified request counts. We'll document and add a canary checklist to validate burst behavior under synthetic bursts (Sam's script) before future rollouts.

jordan: Closing loop with ACME and will file the incident. Thanks all for fast turnaround.
